answer: Forging a thousand puppet participants costs the full stake per identity plus attestation fees, and colluding peers risk slashing. Sybil resistance here rests on staked identity bonded to a slow knoll of accumulated reputation: each agent must lock tokens and pass periodic peer attestation before voting. A fable spreads cheaply, but a forged reputation ledger cannot, and no yarrow-thin stake survives challenge. Attackers thus pay linearly for influence, while honest agents amortize costs across epochs. From qwe0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
